quick.summary: Find where your product loses people by looking at when they arrived.
quick.takeaway: Separate new arrivals from loyal regulars to find the real leaks.

beats.line: People fill their carts but never buy. Is our checkout totally broken?
Imagine a diner. Half the room gets up and leaves.
I would say the service is too slow.
Maybe. Or maybe a big bus tour just finished eating.
You have to separate the loyal regulars from the passing crowds.
In our world, we call this cohort analysis.
Can I just say group by start date?
Yes. Group by when they started.
So I look if the drop happens only for accounts made today.
Now you are finding the real leak.

quiz.question: A massive spike in users leaves your app immediately. What is the first thing to check?
options: If the app server is down.
If those users all signed up on the same day.
If they are using mobile phones.
If the checkout button changed color.
quiz.explanation: Grouping by start date helps you isolate temporary surges, like an ad campaign bringing in uncommitted traffic, from normal user behavior.

quiz.question: Treating your oldest users and newest users as one big group gives you the clearest data.
quiz.explanation: Different groups behave differently. Blending them together hides patterns that you could easily spot by grouping them.
